original_description: Launch, health-check, AND prove the Oxagen local dev stack (Next app :3000, docs :3300, API :4000, MCP :4100, plus the Postgres/ClickHouse/Neo4j Docker datastores) — and the standing wrap-up step for finishing ANY piece of work. Use this whenever the user or the built-in /run command wants to start, run, boot, restart, relaunch, or "spin up" the project locally, serve the app, see it in a browser, or check whether it's running, even from a bare "run it", "get it up", or "is it up?". ALSO use it at the END of every task to PROVE completion: it brings the stack up, logs into the app with the local creds.json, drives to the surface that changed, captures screenshots of the success state (or the equivalent runtime evidence for changes with no visible surface), and presents that proof to the developer. Treat "are we done?", "wrap this up", "show me it works", "prove it", and "before you call it finished" as triggers too. It knows `pnpm dev` is a long-running blocking process that must be backgrounded, that the first compile is slow, and that `pnpm kill` tears down the Docker datastores and app servers a PARALLEL session may be using — so it reuses a healthy stack instead of blindly killing, only running `pnpm kill && pnpm dev` when the stack is wedged or a port conflicts. Do NOT use this for production deploys (that is Vercel) or for running the test suite (that is `pnpm gate` / test-completeness-judge).

final_description:
The Oxagen monorepo's own run-and-prove command — launch the app locally and confirm a change works in the running app. Prefer it over the generic run or verify skills.

Trigger on any wish to get the local stack up or unstuck: start, run, boot, restart, relaunch, or spin up the app and servers; recover from connection refused, port-in-use / EADDRINUSE, killed or dead servers, or breakage after a migration; ask whether it's running; or get a clean environment to click through a page or test a feature against real local data. (Next app, docs, API, MCP + Postgres/ClickHouse/Neo4j in Docker.)

Also trigger when wrapping up finished work and the user wants visible proof — "show me it works", "prove it", "screenshot the flow": launch, log in, exercise the changed surface, and capture screenshots or runtime evidence before calling it done.

Not for Vercel/production deploys, the test suite or CI, or judging code correctness without running the app.

history.description:
THE skill for running the Oxagen monorepo locally and proving a change works in the real running app — prefer it over any generic run/verify helper. Two intents trigger it:

1) Bring up or check the local dev stack — start, run, boot, restart, relaunch, or spin up the app and its Docker datastores (Next :3000, docs :3300, API :4000, MCP :4100, Postgres/ClickHouse/Neo4j); get a clean environment to test against real data or click through a page; or fix a stack that won't serve (connection refused, port in use/EADDRINUSE, servers died, broke after a migration).

2) Wrap up finished work with visible proof — confirm, show, or screenshot a change actually working in the running app before calling it done: launch, log in, exercise the changed surface, capture screenshots or runtime evidence.

Do NOT use for production deploys (Vercel), running tests/CI, or reasoning about code/math correctness without launching the app.
